moment: Communication & conflict
mechanism: State Fact → Remove Approval → Add Nothing
title: DROP THE APPEAL
goal: Reality has already entered the room; the appeal is only in your mind.
steps: 1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove Approval — Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.

Let communication strain be one experience, not your whole identity.

goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.

fullRitual:
ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES

GOAL
Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.

1. Issue Recurring — Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately.
2. Give Own — Give each its own conclusion and action. Say what happened as if you were reporting it.
3. Don't Erase — Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context.

WIN
✓ One fight found its proper scale—without erasing the history or excusing the pattern.

TIPS
• Give a respectful boundary a turn before repeating peak-heat speaking.
• Pause conflict spreading; give a specific request a fair chance.
• Let less damage remain possible even if conflict heat stays.
• Use one clear sentence when communication strain starts feeling permanent.
• Do not turn a difficult conversation into a reason for conflict spreading.

MIND BEND
Your mind can say “today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship” and still leave room for a different next move.

FORMULA FLOW
Issue Recurring → Give Own → Don't Erase

SAFETY
PAUSE
Prioritise present safety regardless of historical positives.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

fullRitual:
THE LOWER PAUSE

GOAL
Hear what was actually said before answering what you feared was meant.

1. Hold Reply — Let your planned response wait.
2. Reflect — Repeat the core message in your own words.
3. Check — Ask whether you understood it correctly.
4. Respond — Answer the confirmed message, not the imagined one.

WIN
✓ The conversation slowed enough for meaning to arrive before defence.

TIPS
• Connection improves when guesses become questions when repeating the same point because you feel unheard in the moment.
• Use the next minute as the size of the problem for now during escalating repetition.
• A useful pause is action when the alternative is automatic reaction while escalating repetition is active.
• Give your nervous system and your judgement different jobs in this escalating repetition moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after repeating the same point because you feel unheard in the moment.
